Rashi on Pesachim 13b:10:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion] - Are you saying that through slaughter alone its physical entity is consecrated, so that it can no longer be redeemed?

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:10:2.english: Slaughter and sprinkling - They permit the sacrifice and that which is dependent upon it.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:10:3.hebrew: מעלין - מעלין אותו מעלה אחת ליקדש בגופו, ואע"פ שאינו ניתר עד שתבוא השניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:10:3.english: Elevate - They elevate it one degree, to become intrinsically consecrated, even though it is not permitted until the second [permitting factor] comes.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:10:4.hebrew: שתי הלחם של עצרת תלויין בשני כבשי שלמים - דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ג:י״ט-כ׳): "ושני כבשים בני שנה לזבח השלמים, והניף הכהן אותם על לחם הבכורים תנופה לפני ה'", וגמרינן להו מלחמי תודה שאין קדושים אלא בזביחתה, במנחות בפרק התכלת:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:10:4.english: The two loaves of Atzeret are dependent upon the two lambs of the peace-offerings - As it is written (Leviticus 23:19–20): "And two yearling lambs for a sacrifice of peace-offerings, and the priest shall wave them with the bread of the first fruits as a wave-offering before the Lord," and we derive them from the loaves of the thanks-offering, which are consecrated only through its slaughter, in Tractate Menachot in the chapter entitled HaTekhelet:

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:11:1.hebrew: קדוש - ליפסל ביוצא, ושלא יפדה עוד:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:11:1.english: Consecrated - To become disqualified by [being taken] outside, and that it may no longer be redeemed.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:11:2.hebrew: ואינו קדוש - ואינו ניתר באכילה. ואף על פי שהכבשים עצמן מותרין — דקיימא לן: כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשירין, אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה; ותניא בפרק שני דביצה (ד' כ:): כבשי עצרת ששחטן שלא לשמן, הדם יזרק והבשר יאכל — אינהו הוא דמתאכלי, כשלמים בעלמא; אבל לחם — כיון דכבשים אין שמן עליהן, דהא לא עלו לשם חובה אלא לשם שלמי נדבה — עליהן מי יתירנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:11:2.english: And it is not consecrated - And it is not permitted to be eaten. And even though the lambs themselves are permitted [to be eaten] — as we maintain: All offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake are valid, but they do not count for the owner toward fulfillment of the obligation; and it is taught in the second chapter of Beitzah (20b): “The lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot] that one slaughtered not for their own sake, the blood shall be sprinkled and the flesh eaten” — it is they [alone] that are eaten, as ordinary peace-offerings; but the bread — since the lambs do not have their [obligatory] designation upon them, for they did not count toward fulfillment of the obligation, but rather as voluntary peace-offerings — upon them, what shall permit it?

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:14:1.hebrew: כאבוה - בב"ק, בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא ד' עו:):
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:14:1.english: In accordance with his father - [This is stated] in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 76b).

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:14:2.english: About to be sprinkled - That it is lacking nothing other than sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:14:3.hebrew: כזרוק דמי - לחול עליו כל שם פסול קדשי קדשים, אבל לאישתרויי לא מישתרי עד דזריק:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:14:3.english: Is considered as sprinkled - For every designation of disqualification of most holy offerings to take effect upon it; but to become permitted [to be eaten], it does not become permitted until he [actually] sprinkles [the blood].

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:1:1.hebrew: בכדי חסרונן - כשאין נחסרין אלא כדרך חסרון של פירות, הקצוב בב"מ בהמפקיד (ב"מ ד' מ.) לחטין ולאורז — תשעה חצאי קבין לכור:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:1:1.english: At the standard rate of their decrease - When they decrease only according to the normal [rate of] loss of produce, which is fixed in Bava Metzia in [the chapter entitled] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 40a) for wheat and for rice — nine half-kavs per kor.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:1:2.english: As it will be entirely lost - For they become forbidden from benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:2:1.english: On the bench - On the actual seat.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:2:2.english: And does he need to conceal them - For are they not placed there to be seen?

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:2:3.english: The roof of the colonnade - A roof was built above [it] on account of the rain:

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:3:1.hebrew: סטיו כפול היה - האיצטבא סביב סביב מקפת, ובתוך אותו הקף עוד אחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:3:1.english: [The Temple Mount] was a double colonnade - The colonnade encircled [it] all around, and within that perimeter [was] another [one].

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:4:1.hebrew: מתוך שהן מרובות - לחמי תודה בשלשה עשר בניסן, שכל מי שיש לו להביא תודה ברגל מביאה בשלשה עשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:4:1.english: Since they are numerous - The loaves of the thanks-offering on the thirteenth of Nisan, for anyone who has to bring a thanks-offering on the Festival brings it on the thirteenth.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:4:2.hebrew: נפסלות בלינה - לבוקרו של י"ד. לחמי תודה — מ' חלות, וי' מהן חמץ, שנא' (ויקרא ז׳:י״ג) "על חלות לחם חמץ":
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:4:2.english: They are disqualified by remaining overnight - [Namely,] by the morning of the fourteenth [of Nisan]. The loaves of a thanks-offering [consist of] forty loaves, and ten of them are leavened bread, as it is stated (Leviticus 7:13): "With cakes of leavened bread."

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:5:1.hebrew: אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול - אין מביאין קרבן ביום שיתמעט זמן אכילתו שקבעה לו תורה, ונמצא בא לידי נותר. ותודה נאכלת ליום ולילה, ואם יביאום בי"ד — אינן נאכלות של חמץ אלא עד שש שעות:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:5:1.english: One may not bring consecrated offerings to a situation of disqualification - One does not bring an offering on a day when the eating time designated for it by the Torah will be curtailed, resulting in it becoming notar [leftover sacrificial food]. And a thanks-offering is eaten for a day and a night, and if they bring them on the fourteenth [of Nisan] — those [loaves] of leaven may be eaten only until six hours [into the day].

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:6:1.hebrew: וכולי עלמא בי"ג מייתי להו - כל מי שעליו תודה מביאה בי"ג, לפי שלא יקריבנה למחר, וכ"ש בפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:6:1.english: And everyone brings them on the thirteenth - Whoever has [an obligation to bring] a thanks-offering brings it on the thirteenth [of Nisan], because he may not sacrifice it tomorrow [on the fourteenth], and all the more so on Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:6:2.hebrew: נפסלות בלינה - שאין להם אוכלין כל כך. ומשום דפסולות ועומדות היו ניתנין שם, דאם היו כשירות, לא היו נותנין אותן שם כדי לפוסלן בידים — שמונחות שם עד זמן הביעור ונשרפות:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:6:2.english: They are disqualified by being left overnight - Because they do not have that many people to eat them. And because they were already disqualified, they were placed there; for if they were fit, they would not place them there so as to actively disqualify them, as they lie there until the time of removal and are burned.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:7:1.hebrew: כשירות היו - כלומר, אפילו לא היה להן פסול גדול כלינה שהן כבר לשריפה, אפ"ה מאחר שאין להם תקנה ליאכל, ואפילו הן עדיין טעונות עיבור צורה — יהבינן להו התם. והיכי דמי? כגון שלא נשחט עליהן הזבח, ויש להן קדושת דמים משהוקדשו, ואין להן היתר עד שישחט עליהן הזבח ויזרק הדם; דלחמי תודה אין קדושין קדושת הגוף אלא בשחיטת הזבח, כדתניא במנחות: "על חלות לחם חמץ יקריב קרבנו על זבח" — מלמד שאין הלחם קדוש אלא בזביחת התודה. והאי "קדוש", קדושת הגוף קאמר, דהא משעה שאמר "הרי (עלי) לתודתי" חל עליהם שם הקדש, אבל אין קדושות ליפסל בלינה ובטבול יום, ואם נטמאו נפדין ויוצאין לחולין עד שישחט הזבח עליהן. וכשם שהזבח מקדשן, כך בזריקת הדם ניתרין הם לאכילה כבשר התודה עצמו, דהואיל ותלויין בה הרי היא כמוה, וזריקת הדם מתרת קדשים, דכתיב: "ודם זבחיך ישפך", והדר: "והבשר תאכל":
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:7:1.english: They were fit - That is to say, even though they did not have a severe disqualification such as [having been left] overnight, which would make them already [designated] for burning, nevertheless, since they have no remedy to be eaten, and even though they still require alteration of form [ibbur tzurah, being left overnight to become unfit], we place them there. And what is the case? For example, where the sacrifice was not slaughtered over them, and they possess sanctity of value from when they were consecrated, but they have no permit [to be eaten] until the sacrifice is slaughtered over them and the blood is sprinkled. For the loaves of a thanks-offering do not become consecrated with intrinsic sanctity except with the slaughter of the sacrifice, as it was taught in a baraita in Menachot: “With cakes of leavened bread he shall present his offering with the sacrifice” [Leviticus 7:13] — this teaches that the bread does not become consecrated except with the slaughter of the thanks-offering. And this [statement that it becomes] “consecrated” means [consecrated with] intrinsic sanctity; for from the moment he said, “Behold, [these are (incumbent upon me)] for my thanks-offering,” the status of consecration took effect upon them, but they are not consecrated [to the extent that they would] become disqualified by [being left] overnight or by one who immersed that day [a tevul yom], and if they become defiled, they may be redeemed and go out to non-sacred status, until the sacrifice is slaughtered over them. And just as the sacrifice consecrates them, so with the sprinkling of the blood they are permitted for eating, like the meat of the thanks-offering itself; for since they are dependent upon it, it is like it. And the sprinkling of the blood permits sacrificial [foods], as it is written: “And the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out,” and afterwards: “and the meat you may eat” [Deuteronomy 12:27].

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:8:1.hebrew: אין מביא תודה אחרת - על אותו לחם; ופודין אותו ויוצא לחולין, דלחם גלל תודה, וכיון דהוקבע לזו — פסול לאחרת. אבל בדמים יקח תודה, או לחם תודה אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:8:1.english: One does not bring another thanks-offering - For that [same] bread. And one redeems it and it becomes unconsecrated, for bread is [brought] on account of the thanks-offering, and since it was designated for this [animal], it is disqualified for another. But with the [redemption] money, he shall purchase a thanks-offering, or bread for another thanks-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:8:2.english: And the thanks-offering is not [brought] on account of the loaves - For it is the primary [component].

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:9:1.hebrew: ונפרקינהו - דכל זמן שלא קידשו לגופן יש להם פדיון, והואיל ויש להם תקנה בכך, למה אנו מפסידין קדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:9:1.english: And let us redeem them - For as long as they have not attained bodily sanctity, they can be redeemed; and since they have a remedy in this [manner], why should we cause consecrated items to be lost?

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:9:2.english: Rather, actually, where the offering was slaughtered over them - For they no longer have any remedy.

Rashi on Pesachim 13b:9:3.hebrew: וכגון שנשפך הדם - ומיהו עדיין אינן טעונות שריפה, וצריכות לעבר צורתן; דתנן בכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים פב.): כל שפסולו בגופו — ישרף מיד, בדם ובבעלים — תעובר צורתו ויצא לבית השריפה. ואפ"ה מזלזלינן בהו ויהבינן להו התם:
Rashi on Pesachim 13b:9:3.english: And, for example, where the blood was spilled - However, they still do not require burning, and they need their form to become altered; as we learned in the chapter entitled Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 82a): "Whatever has its disqualification in its body shall be burned immediately; whatever has its disqualification in the blood or in the owners, its form must become altered and it shall go out to the place of burning." And even so, we treat them lightly and place them there.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:11:1.hebrew: שחטן שלא לשמן ונזרק דמן שלא לשמן - נראה: "נזרק דמן שלא לשמן" לאו דוקא, דהוא הדין אם נזרק לשמן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:11:1.english: "One slaughtered them not for their sake and their blood was sprinkled not for their sake" - It appears that "their blood was sprinkled not for their sake" is not specific, for the same law applies if it was sprinkled for their sake.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:11:2.hebrew: הלחם קדוש - בהתכלת (מנחות ד' מז:) איכא מאן דאמר: קדוש לתפוס פדיונו. ולא בעי למימר שיצא לחולין, אלא תופס פדיונו ואינו יוצא לחולין — דאל"כ, אכתי תיקשי: וליפרקינהו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:11:2.english: "The loaves are consecrated" - In [the chapter entitled] HaTekhelet (Menachot 47b), there is one who says [that this means it is] consecrated to confer sanctity upon its redemption [money]. And he does not mean to say that [the bread] goes out to non-sacred status [upon redemption]; rather, it confers sanctity upon its redemption [money], but does not go out to non-sacred status [itself]. For if that were not so, it would still be difficult: Let us redeem them!

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:14:1.hebrew: כל העומד ליזרק כזרוק דמי - וא"ת: זרק דמן שלא לשמן, נימא נמי "כזרוק דמי", ואמאי קאמר רבי אלעזר ב"ר שמעון דאינו קדוש? וי"ל: כיון שעקרן מלשמן — גרע מנשפך הדם, ואיגליא מלתא דלא הוי כזרוק בשעת קבלה. וקשה, דבפרק המנחות והנסכים (מנחות קב.) אמר: פיגל בזריקה — מטמא טומאת אוכלים לר"ש, משום דכל העומד ליזרוק כזרוק דמי; ודוחק לחלק בין פיגול לשלא לשמו! וי"ל: דלגביה גופיה דזבח חשיב כזרוק, אע"ג דפיגל בזריקה; אבל לגבי דברים המתקדשים עם הזבח, כגון לחם — לא חשיב כזרוק כשנעשה הזריקה שלא בהכשר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:14:1.english: Any [blood] that is about to be sprinkled is considered as sprinkled - And if you say: [If] he sprinkled their blood not for their own sake, let us also say [that the blood is] "considered as sprinkled," so why did Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, say that [the bread] is not consecrated? And one can say: Since he uprooted them from their [intended] purpose, it is worse than [if] the blood spilled, and the matter became revealed [in retrospect] that it was not [considered] as sprinkled at the time of receiving. And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] HaMenachot VeHaNesakhim (Menachot 102a), [the Gemara] says: [If] one rendered [the offering] piggul during sprinkling, it contracts the ritual impurity of food according to Rabbi Shimon, because whatever is about to be sprinkled is considered as sprinkled; and it is forced to distinguish between piggul and [sprinkling] not for its own sake! And one can say: Regarding the sacrifice itself, it is considered as sprinkled even though he rendered it piggul during sprinkling; but regarding items that are consecrated along with the sacrifice, such as bread, it is not considered as sprinkled when the sprinkling was performed improperly.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:15:1.hebrew: כשירות היו - וא"ת: מאחר דכשירות היו, אמאי משהין אותן עד שעת איסור? וי"ל: דהיינו (כרשב"ג) דאמר לעיל (פסחים ד' יא:): תרומה כל חמש, ולחמי תודה כתרומה; והיו נוטלים האחרונה בסוף חמש. וכן משמע בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:15:1.english: "They were fit" - And if you say: Since they were fit, why do they leave them until the time of prohibition? And one can say that this is (in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel), who said above (Pesachim 11b): Teruma [may be eaten throughout] the fifth [hour], and the loaves of the thanksgiving offering are like teruma; and they would remove the latter [loaf] at the end of the fifth [hour]. And this is also indicated in the Yerushalmi.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:1:1.hebrew: בכדי חסרונן - פ"ה: כדרך חסרונם של פירות. וקשה לר"י: א"כ, מ"ט דרשב"ג דאמר מוכרן בב"ד? ואור"י: דמיירי דנחסר בחדש אחד יותר ממה שחסרון עולה לחדש, וקרי "בכדי חסרונן" לפי שעדיין לא נתחסרו יותר מכדי חסרון העולה לשנה, כדמפר' בהמפקיד (ב"מ מ.): "לחטין ולאורז תשעה חצאי קבין לכור". אבל אם נחסרו יותר — ד"ה מוכרן בב"ד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:1:1.english: At the standard rate of their decrease - The Kuntras explained: In accordance with the normal rate of decrease of produce. And the Ri questions [this]: If so, what is the reasoning of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said that he sells them in court? And the Ri says: [The mishna] is dealing with [a case] where it decreased in one month by more than what the decrease amounts to for a month, and it calls [this] "at the standard rate of their decrease" because they have not yet decreased by more than the amount of decrease that accrues for a year, as [the mishna] explains in [the chapter] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 40a): "For wheat and for rice, nine half-kavs per kor." However, if they decreased more [than that], all agree that he sells them in court.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:3:1.hebrew: אמר רחבא אמר רבי יהודה - לפי שהיה רבו מובהק, קרי לי' ר':
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:3:1.english: "Raḥava said that Rabbi Yehuda said" - Because he was his primary teacher, he calls him "Rabbi" [rather than "Rav"].

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:8:1.hebrew: אין מביאין תודה אחרת - פ"ה: ואותו לחם פודים ויוצא לחולין, ויקח בדמים תודה אחרת או לחם לתודה אחרת. ואין נראה, כיון דלחם גופיה לא חזי לתודה אחרת — דמים נמי לא חזו לתודה אחרת, דמאי שנא? ובפרק התודה (מנחות פ.) אמר בהדיא: הפריש מעות ללחמי תודה וניתותרו — אין מביא בהן תודה אחרת. ואע"ג דהדמים אסורים, פריך שפיר: וניפרקינהו — דשמא תמצא תודה שאבדה; א"נ, ניפרקינהו בשוה פרוטה, דלכתחלה יכול לחלל שוה מנה על פרוטה כשאין הפסד להקדש, כדמוכח בערכין (ד' כט.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:8:1.english: One does not bring another thanks-offering - Rashi explained: And that bread is redeemed and becomes non-sacred, and with the money one should purchase another thanks-offering or bread for another thanks-offering. And this does not appear correct, since the bread itself is not fit for another thanks-offering, the money is also not fit for another thanks-offering; for what is the difference? And in the chapter entitled "HaTodah" (Menachot 80a), it explicitly states: If one designated money for the loaves of a thanks-offering and money remained over, he may not bring another thanks-offering with them. And even though the money is forbidden for non-sacred use, the Gemara rightly asks: "And let us redeem them," for perhaps the thanks-offering that was lost will be found; alternatively, let us redeem them for the value of a perutah, for ab initio one can deconsecrate the value of a maneh onto a perutah when there is no financial loss to the Temple treasury, as is proven in Arakhin (29a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:9:1.hebrew: אלא לעולם שנשחט עליהן הזבח - אומר ריב"א: דהשתא הדר ביה ממה שאמר "כשירות היו", דבי"ג איירי שנשחט הזבח, כדאמר לעיל "אין מביאין תודה בי"ד"; והשתא מיפסלו טפי, שנשפך הדם וגם נפסלו בלינה. ולכך מעמיד בנשפך הדם — שהטעם הראשון שאמר רבי חנינא, "מתוך שהן מרובות נפסלות בלינה", נראה לו דוחק; דאיך יתכן דמפני ריבוי שלהן לא ימצא אוכלים? הלא מותרין לזרים! ובירושלמי, רבי חנינא גופיה משני האי שינויא, דגרס התם: "רבי חנינא אומר: פסולות היו, מפני שהיו ממהרים להביא תודותיהן מפני חמץ שבתודות, ואי אפשר שלא ישפך דמה של אחת מהן והן נפסלות". מדקאמר "מפני שממהרין", משמע דבי"ג מיירי, דכולם היו מביאין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13b:9:1.english: Rather, actually, where the offering was slaughtered over them - Riva says that now [the Gemara] retracts from what it had said [earlier], that "they were fit" — for it is dealing with [a case where] the offering was slaughtered on the thirteenth [of Nisan], as [the Gemara] stated above, "One does not bring a thanks-offering on the fourteenth"; and now they are all the more disqualified, [both because] the blood spilled and [because] they also became disqualified by [being left] overnight. And therefore [the Gemara] establishes [the case as one where] the blood spilled, because the first reason that Rabbi Chanina stated — "since they are numerous, they become disqualified by [being left] overnight" — seemed forced to it; for how could it be that due to their abundance, eaters could not be found? Are they not permitted to non-priests! And in the Yerushalmi, Rabbi Chanina himself gives this resolution, as the text there reads: "Rabbi Chanina says: They were disqualified, because they would rush to bring their thanks-offerings on account of the leaven in the thanks-offerings, and it is impossible that the blood of [at least] one of them would not spill, and [consequently] they become disqualified." From [the fact] that it says "because they rush," this implies that it is dealing with the thirteenth [of Nisan], when everyone would bring [their thanks-offerings].
